evidence_type: direct target in zebrafish (cycloheximide-resistant BMP induction); BMP-responsive element in the mouse Smad6 promoter

evidence_type: direct target in zebrafish (cycloheximide-resistant BMP induction); BMP-responsive element in the mouse Smad6 promoter

evidence_type: positive autoregulation through a Nodal response element (FoxH1/Smad) in the squint first intron (transgenic reporters)
other_identity: maternal transcript; dorsal margin; dorsal forerunner cells; YSL

evidence_type: Nodal ligands induce their own transcription (positive autoregulatory loop), stated for both zebrafish Nodals
other_identity: margin, then shield hypoblast, axial mesoderm, left LPM and left diencephalon
notes: cyclops. No ndr2-specific enhancer or loss-of-function test was found; the general autoregulation statement is the only evidence. Later expression marks axial mesoderm and laterality.

evidence_type: direct target (Tcf/Lef sites in the promoter and intron; rapid induction by Wnt), mouse
notes: Evidence is from mouse; no zebrafish primary report checked. Widely used as a generic Wnt/beta-catenin readout.

evidence_type: expression mirrors Wnt/beta-catenin activity (ventrolateral margin, axial mesendoderm); Nkd1 inhibits canonical Wnt
notes: Wnt induction was inferred from expression, not tested directly. nkd1 is also a direct BMP target (greenfeld2021, cluster 4), so it is not specific to Wnt.
program_note: readout of several pathways (also a BMP target)

evidence_type: Wnt/beta-catenin-induced secreted inhibitor (self-regulatory loop; Wnt gain and loss in zebrafish)
direct Wnt target through a Wnt-responsive element in the LEF-1 promoter (human cells); in zebrafish Lef1 drives the TOPdGFP Wnt reporter
other_identity: margin and tailbud (identity marker for posterior mesoderm/tailbud); neural crest
notes: The direct-target evidence is from mammalian cells. dorsky2002 shows that Lef1 is needed for reporter activity, not that lef1 expression depends on Wnt. lef1 is also a strong identity marker, so it confounds Wnt activity with tailbud and margin identity.

evidence_type: induced by FGF (gain and loss of FGF signalling), mouse and chick
notes: No zebrafish primary report checked for spry2.

evidence_type: FGF feedback-induced antagonist: lost in ace/fgf8 mutants and with SU5402, induced by FGF8
induced by FGF (vertebrate Sprouty family), mouse and chick
notes: No zebrafish primary report checked for spry1.

evidence_type: FGF synexpression; under FGF control after initiation by maternal beta-catenin on the dorsal side; FGF reporter transgene

evidence_type: lost in fgf8 mutants and with SU5402; induced by ectopic fgf8
notes: pea3; expressed close to FGF sources (narrower range than erm).

evidence_type: lost in fgf8 mutants and with SU5402; induced by ectopic fgf8
notes: erm; broader domain than pea3.

evidence_type: FGF synexpression; positively regulated by FGF; feedback inhibitor of Ras/MAPK
notes: sef.

other_identity: presumptive anterior neural ectoderm and margin (gastrula), tailbud (identity markers)
notes: Inducible by RA, but its endogenous gastrula pattern is mostly RA-independent (dobbsmcauliffe2004) and is repressed by FGF and Wnt (kudoh2002), so in untreated embryos it reads anterior identity, not RA activity. The evidence for responsiveness alone would be strong; it is moderate as a readout.
program_note: expressed where RA is degraded (anterior neural plate, tailbud), not with dhrs3a

evidence_type: RA-dependent and strongly RA-inducible (microarray: opposite response to RA and RA antagonist; in situ)
notes: Shown at early somite stages; responsiveness before bud not tested.

other_identity: neural plate (primary neurogenesis domains) and hypoblast
notes: The her4 cluster (her4.1-her4.5) is a tandem duplication; the studies used her4 probes and enhancers that do not resolve the copies.

evidence_type: as HER15.1
notes: As HER15.1.

evidence_type: PSM expression regulated by Delta-Notch (mutants, morpholinos, inhibitor), complex

evidence_type: direct Notch target (Xenopus: Su(H)-dependent induction); zebrafish nrarpa also stabilises Lef1 (Wnt)

program_note: readout of several pathways (also acts in Wnt/Lef1 signalling)

evidence_type: direct Notch target (Xenopus); direct BMP target in zebrafish (cycloheximide)
notes: Also a direct BMP target (greenfeld2021, cluster 4), so not specific to Notch at gastrula stages.
program_note: readout of several pathways (also a BMP target)

evidence_type: dynamic PSM expression impaired in deltaD (after-eight) mutants; ectopic deltaD induces hey1; promoter is a direct Notch target in mouse and human

evidence_type: transcription follows shh activity; ectopic shh activates it; PKA-dependent
other_identity: cells near the midline, from about bud stage
notes: Nomenclature: zebrafish ptch2 is the gene called patched1/ptc1 in concordet1996 and lewis1999.

evidence_type: Shh activates Gli1 transcription (Xenopus); in zebrafish Gli1 (detour) is an activator of Hh target genes
notes: Induction by Hh is shown in frog. karlstrom2003 shows gli1 is required for Hh target genes, not that it is induced by Hh.

evidence_type: induced by ectopic Hh and lost in Hh mutants (mouse); zebrafish hhip is expressed in Hh-responding adaxial cells
notes: Induction is shown in mouse; ochi2006 shows zebrafish hhip expression in Hh-responding cells and its function, not regulation.

evidence_type: IFN-stimulated gene (induced by recombinant type I IFN and by virus via IFNR in larvae); also induced by morpholino injection
notes: Expected to be uniform: no infection, and the immune system develops after this window (first macrophages arise from mesoderm in the somite stages, herbomel1999; adaptive immunity weeks later, lam2004). lai2019 shows ISGs are induced by morpholinos and cell stress, so variation may be technical.

evidence_type: IFN-stimulated gene (larvae, recombinant IFN and virus)
notes: As ISG15.

evidence_type: IFN-stimulated gene (viperin; larvae, recombinant IFN and virus)
notes: As ISG15.

evidence_type: AHR target induced by TCDD and PCB126 in embryos (xenobiotic response elements)
notes: Without an AHR agonist cyp1a is low. Even after TCDD from 3-4 hpf, CYP1A mRNA was first seen at about 24 hpf in vasculature (andreasen2002), so no induced AHR response is expected at 3-12 hpf.

evidence_type: induced by PCB126 in embryos (xenobiotic response elements)
other_identity: endogenous expression in eye and heart (later stages)
notes: jonsson2007 suggests endogenous developmental roles (eye, heart). Check that it does not mark a population in the atlas before using it as a control.

evidence_type: induced by PCB126 in embryos; high basal embryonic expression
other_identity: endogenous expression in eye and heart (later stages)
notes: Higher basal expression in embryos than cyp1a (jonsson2007), so it may carry developmental signal.

evidence_type: induced by TCDD in ZF-L cells and embryos; AHR negative-feedback repressor
notes: ahrr2 in evans2005 (ahrra/ahrr1 is not in the atlas). Both AHRRs have basal embryonic expression.

evidence_type: GR target: up-regulated by full-length GR mRNA at 6 hpf; GR-dependent and cortisol-induced in larvae
notes: Embryonic cortisol is maternal, falling from 1.5 hpf to hatching; the interrenal stress axis matures only after hatching (alsop2008). GR activity at 3-12 hpf should therefore be low and embryo-wide.

evidence_type: under-expressed in GR mutant larvae and induced by cortisol; feedforward regulator of fkbp5
notes: klf9 is also a classic thyroid-hormone target, so it is not GR-specific.

evidence_type: described as a GR target (gilz) with GR-dependent daily oscillation in larvae
notes: Evidence comes from a single statement in gans2021; no direct induction experiment was checked.

evidence_type: zygotic period1 transcription requires CLOCK (dominant-negative CLOCK blocks it)
notes: Caveat: dekens2008 reports that per1 oscillations start autonomously and are asynchronous between cells in embryos kept in the dark. Under a light-dark cycle the cells should be synchronised, but per1b may vary between cells in this window. per1b is assumed to be the period1 of dekens2008.

evidence_type: light-induced in all zebrafish cells through a D-box/E-box light-responsive module; light at 0-6 hpf transiently raises per2
notes: Light acts directly on every cell, so the response should be uniform within an embryo pool. It can differ between libraries collected at different times of day.

evidence_type: light-induced clock repressor (cry1a); induction correlates with clock resetting
notes: Studied in cells and larvae; light induction is cell-autonomous. Assumes atlas CRY1AA = cry1a of tamai2007 (renamed after the cry1a duplication was resolved).

evidence_type: light-inducible D-box factor that drives per2 light induction
notes: Assumes atlas TEFA is the tef of vatine2009.

evidence_type: immediate-early gene induced by enzymatic dissociation at 37 C (scRNA-seq), mouse
notes: This is technical variation from cell preparation, not a pathway, and it is expected to vary between cells and correlate with dissociation stress. Use it to flag cells, not as a uniform control. Evidence is from mouse tissues; the zebrafish ortholog is assumed.

evidence_type: immediate-early gene induced by dissociation (mouse)
notes: As FOSAB.

notes: As FOSAB.

notes: As FOSAB. ier2 is not in the atlas.

evidence_type: in situ: maternal, then blastoderm margin at blastula; dorsal blastomeres at MBT and dorsal YSL, whole margin and YSL in early gastrula, dorsal forerunner cells at shield; sqt;cyc double mutants lack organizer, mesoderm and endoderm; misexpression (also only in the YSL) expands organizer fates; Squint/Cyclops required in the YSL for endoderm and head mesoderm
other_identity: margin; dorsal_organizer; YSL; dorsal forerunner cells
notes: squint (znr2 in erter1998). Also a Nodal target (autoregulation through an intronic Nodal response element; see the readout row). The YSL source is removed with the yolk in these embryos.

evidence_type: in situ: blastoderm margin at blastula; dorsal mesendoderm and shield hypoblast at gastrula, prechordal plate until early somitogenesis, later left lateral plate and left diencephalon; cyc mutants lack floor plate and ventral brain, rescued non-autonomously by cyc RNA; redundant with sqt for organizer and mesendoderm
other_identity: margin; dorsal_organizer; prechordal_plate; axial_mesoderm; lateral_plate (left, somitogenesis)
notes: cyclops. Also a Nodal target (see the readout row). rebagliati1998 also reports expression in the anterior neurectoderm overlying the axial mesoderm.

evidence_type: in situ: whole blastula, restricted ventrally before gastrulation (Fgf-dependent); ventral gastrula; swirl/bmp2b mutants dorsalized (loss of non-neural ectoderm, neural crest, ventral mesoderm), cell non-autonomous; overexpression ventralizes
notes: swirl. Main early DV ligand together with bmp7a (heterodimers proposed, schmid2000). Bmp signalling continues in ventral/posterior mesoderm after gastrulation (pyati2005).

evidence_type: in situ: ventral gastrula and also the embryonic shield; null mutants affect late-gastrula specification of ventroposterior fates
notes: Required in the later (late gastrula) phase, not for early DV patterning (stickney2007). Shield expression means it is not a pure ventral marker.

evidence_type: snailhouse/bmp7 mutants strongly dorsalized, null identical to swirl/bmp2b; Bmp2b/Bmp7 synergize (likely heterodimers), transduced by Smad5 and antagonized by Chordino; Bmp genes expressed in the whole blastula, then restricted ventrally
notes: snailhouse. The expression statement in the cited abstracts is for the Bmp genes jointly (furthauer2004), not bmp7a alone.

evidence_type: in situ: dorsal only, from blastula in the organizer region (anterior neuroectoderm and axial mesoderm precursors), vanishing in an anterior-to-posterior wave during gastrulation; also tail organizer; knockdown enlarges the organizer and impairs ventral/posterior development, overexpression is Bmp-like; cooperates with Bmp2b/Bmp7
notes: BMP-family ligand produced on the dorsal (organizer) side, opposite to the other BMP ligands. Maintenance needs Nodal and Bozozok.

evidence_type: in situ: maternal and zygotic; blastoderm margin at 50% epiboly (cleared from the dorsal midline in late gastrula), tailbud during segmentation; deficiency and morpholino: DV mesoderm and AP neural patterning defects; wnt3a/wnt8 double knockdown expands the organizer and removes the posterior body
notes: Called wnt8 in older papers; bicistronic locus (two ORFs). Maternal transcript present in early stages. Redundant with wnt3a.

evidence_type: in situ: blastoderm margin (overlapping wnt8) and later tailbud; wnt3a/wnt8 double knockdown anteriorizes the neuroectoderm, expands the organizer and blocks tail formation; sp5l in the tail depends on wnt3a and wnt8
notes: Single knockdown is milder than the double; redundant with wnt8a.

evidence_type: maternal and zygotic at all gastrula stages; pipetail mutants: cell elongation and convergent extension defects in posterior regions of the gastrula (redundant with wnt11 anteriorly); Frizzled-2 acts downstream
notes: pipetail (ppt/wnt5). Non-canonical Wnt; regulates movement, not fate; no readouts measured. The spatial domain is not given in the abstract.

evidence_type: in situ: blastoderm margin (presumptive mesoderm) from late blastula, induced by the yolk cell and FGF, independent of ntl; later somites and notochord; silberblick mutants: convergent extension defects and cyclopia, cell non-autonomous, rescued by a Dishevelled that does not signal through the canonical pathway
notes: silberblick. Non-canonical Wnt; no readouts measured. ZFIN may list it under a newer symbol (wnt11f2), so match through aliases.

evidence_type: in situ: dorsoventral gradient (dorsal high) at the gastrula margin, not in axial mesoderm; mesodermal precursors; MHB and somitogenesis domains; overexpression dorsalizes and represses ventral bmp2b/bmp4; acerebellar mutants lose the MHB organizer, with mild DV and mesoderm defects; with fgf24 required for posterior mesoderm
notes: acerebellar. Fgf activity spreads from the dorsal side before gastrulation and restricts Bmp expression ventrally (furthauer2004).

evidence_type: in situ: co-expressed with fgf8 in mesodermal precursors during gastrulation; fgf24 knockdown in fgf8 mutants blocks most posterior mesoderm
notes: Dispensable alone; redundant with fgf8a.

evidence_type: in situ: dorsolateral margin from late blastula to early gastrula; overexpression expands the neural region and suppresses anterior neural fate, with little mesoderm-inducing activity
notes: Functional evidence is overexpression only in this reference.

evidence_type: in situ: posterior notochord and Kupffer's vesicle region in early segmentation; knockdown randomizes visceral left-right patterning, removes lefty1 in the posterior notochord and impairs Kupffer's vesicle cilia
other_identity: notochord (posterior); tailbud; dorsal forerunner cells / Kupffer's vesicle
notes: Expression reported only from early segmentation (end of the atlas window); gastrula expression not established here. Morpholino only.

evidence_type: in situ: involuting mesoderm during gastrulation, later paraxial mesoderm, branchial arches, eyes and fin buds; neckless and no-fin (raldh2) mutants: hindbrain/spinal cord AP defects and no pectoral fin, rescued by RA; RA from paraxial mesoderm acts non-autonomously on the neural tube
notes: Retinaldehyde dehydrogenase 2 (raldh2); marks RA-producing cells. Repressed by RA (feedback; dobbsmcauliffe2004); expressed adjacent or opposite to cyp26a1.

evidence_type: in situ: large patches of contiguous cells in the neural plate (with deltaD) within which primary neurons are singled out; misexpression delivers lateral inhibition; itself repressed by lateral inhibition
notes: deltaA.

evidence_type: in situ: scattered cells within the deltaA/deltaD neural plate patches that become primary neurons; misexpression delivers lateral inhibition
notes: deltaB; marks nascent primary neurons more specifically than dla/dld.

evidence_type: in situ: mesoderm from 50% epiboly, tailbud, stripes in the presomitic mesoderm, posterior half of each somite, notochord; also retina, ear and scattered epidermal cells; oscillates in the PSM; beamter/deltaC mutants and morphants disrupt the segmentation clock (her1 oscillation)
notes: beamter. Oscillating expression: single-cell snapshots mix clock phases. Not expressed in most nascent primary neurons.

evidence_type: in situ: neural plate patches (with deltaA) and somite development; misexpression delivers lateral inhibition; after eight (aei)/deltaD mutants lose her1 oscillation in the PSM; deltaD itself does not oscillate
notes: after eight.

evidence_type: in situ: notochord, floor plate (ventral midline of neural tube and brain, incl. ventral diencephalon) and fin mesoderm; ectopic expression consistent with floor plate induction and promotes proximal eye fates; sonic-you mutants: defects in somite patterning, lateral floor plate, fins and motor axons (medial floor plate still forms)
notes: sonic-you. Hedgehog readouts (ptch, gli1) are never heterogeneous in the atlas, so the receiving side cannot be checked.

evidence_type: in situ: ventral midline of neural tube and brain incl. floor of the diencephalon, not notochord; ectopic expression promotes proximal eye fates; lost with the ventral forebrain in cyclops mutants
notes: tiggy-winkle hedgehog (twhh). Neural only; functional evidence is overexpression.

evidence_type: overexpression abolishes mesoderm induction, suppressed by Cyclops/Squint or Activin; expression depends on Nodal (feedback); midline expression overlapping cyc/sqt, later left diencephalon; lft1+lft2 knockdown: unchecked Nodal signalling, expanded mesendoderm and loss of ectoderm; lft1 alone: left-right defects
other_identity: margin; dorsal_organizer; axial_mesoderm (midline); forebrain (left diencephalon, somitogenesis)
notes: antivin. Also a Nodal readout (feedback target; see the readout row).

evidence_type: midline expression overlapping cyc/sqt, later left lateral plate; lft2 knockdown alone has no obvious phenotype, lft1+lft2 knockdown expands mesendoderm through unchecked Squint signalling
notes: Also a Nodal readout (see the readout row). Redundant with lft1 during gastrulation.

evidence_type: in situ: organizer and transiently axial mesoderm, also paraxial mesoderm, ectoderm and brain regions; domains expand in dorsalized mutants by mid-gastrula; overexpression dorsalizes; chordino (dino) mutants ventralized
notes: chordino. Main organizer BMP antagonist; its later domains are repressed by BMP, so lateral chd also reflects low BMP.

evidence_type: noggin1 expressed in the fish organizer and dorsalizes on overexpression; all three zebrafish noggins antagonize ventralizing BMPs
notes: bauer1998 reports that noggin is not expressed in the organizer and has no patterned expression during gastrulation; which paralog they cloned is not stated in the abstract, so organizer expression of nog1 is contested. No loss-of-function evidence verified.

evidence_type: overexpression antagonizes ventralizing BMPs; expression differs from noggin1/noggin3 (domain not stated in the abstract)
notes: Expression at the atlas stages not verified; function from overexpression only.

evidence_type: in situ: from mid-gastrula in anterior paraxial mesoderm (head mesoderm and first five somites), transient in the posterior notochord anlage, later brain, eyes and somites; excluded from the organizer; domain regulated by Bmp2b and Chordino; overexpression dorsalizes like Xenopus follistatin
other_identity: mesoderm (anterior paraxial, head mesoderm, first somites); notochord (posterior anlage, transient)
notes: Called follistatin in bauer1998 (fsta assumed). Proposed to refine late DV patterning, not to act as an organizer signal. Follistatin can also bind activin-like ligands (not verified for zebrafish).

evidence_type: in situ: ventral from late blastula through gastrula, posterior end during segmentation; ogon mutants/morphants ventralized; overexpression dorsalizes, needs Chordin; does not inhibit Wnt8-dependent transcription
notes: ogon/sizzled. A BMP feedback target (see the readout row): expressed where BMP is high, while acting to limit BMP.

evidence_type: in situ: dorsal marginal blastoderm and dorsal YSL after MBT, entire margin at late blastula, embryonic shield during gastrulation, then anterior axial mesendoderm (prospective prechordal plate); maintenance reduced in boz, sqt and oep mutants; overexpression enlarges forebrain, eyes and axial mesendoderm
notes: Called dkk1 in hashimoto2000dkk1 (ZFIN dkk1b). Functional evidence is overexpression only. Maintenance depends on Nodal.

evidence_type: sfrp3 (frzb) cloned; expressed mainly in mesodermal and endodermal tissues (stages not given in the abstract)
notes: frzb = sfrp3. Gastrula expression and Wnt antagonism in zebrafish not verified.

evidence_type: in situ: anterior neural plate including the anterior neural border cells (with tlc), complementary to posterior wnt expression; later ventral forebrain, midbrain and hindbrain; sfrp1a loss of function upregulates canonical Wnt signalling (hematopoietic stem cells)
notes: Functional evidence is from hematopoiesis, long after 12 hpf; Sfrps can also act as Wnt agonists (ide2026).

evidence_type: in situ: presumptive anterior neural ectoderm and blastoderm margin from late blastula, circumblastoporal ring during gastrulation, tailbud during somitogenesis; complementary to hoxb1b; knockdown or giraffe mutation expands posterior (spinal cord) fates; encodes the RA 4-hydroxylase
notes: Also an RA readout (RA-inducible; see the readout row), but also repressed by Fgf and Wnt (kudoh2002) and directly activated by Ntl in mesodermal progenitors (martin2010), so it marks an RA sink more than RA level.
